findings.quote: The education savings account program is repealed
findings.mechanism: Eliminates the state program that administers education savings accounts.

analysis.answer: Current law provides parents with an education savings account funded at 90 percent of the state's per-pupil amount to use for private education expenses. The measure eliminates this program in 2028 and sends unspent funds back to the state public school system.

Families who currently use or plan to use the accounts for private tuition, tutoring, or homeschooling bear the cost of losing state subsidies. Public school districts benefit from retaining full per-pupil funding and receiving the reverted funds.

Families unable to afford private tuition or alternative educational costs without the subsidy may re-enroll their children in the public school system. Private schools and educational service providers may see reduced enrollment or revenue.
Public school districts gain resources, while private educational service providers and parents seeking state-funded alternatives to public school lose financial support.
The repeal is statutory and features a delayed effective date (2028), giving future legislatures time to modify, reverse, or replace the measure before the program ends.

flags.note: The repeal features a delayed effective date.

items.text: Resources and funding stability for public school systems, including the return of unspent private-account funds.
